title: CI 'zig build test' retry loop (.github/workflows/ci.yml) can report exit 0 / job PASS even though the underlying zig build test run printed a 'failed command:' line — retry loop's status==0 check is not trustworthy evidence of a real pass
registered_by: WF-03 GH #443 fix verification (PR #447 CI run review)
scope: .github/workflows/ci.yml 'zig build test' step's bounded-retry loop (added for ISS-0136/GH #436). Discovered reviewing the CI log for PR #447's 'Build and unit tests' job (run 31033090698, job 92398360577) after merge -- the job reported overall PASS in 5m33s, but its own step log shows attempt 2 produced the same truncated 'failed command: .../test --cache-dir=... --seed=... --listen=-' signature as attempt 1 (which the loop correctly identified as a timeout, exit 124), yet the loop's own status check treated attempt 2 as a clean pass (status==0, loop exits immediately, no 'attempt 2 failed' message printed) and moved straight to the next CI step.
symptom: In the PR #447 CI log for 'Build and unit tests' > 'zig build test': attempt 1 printed 16x 'BPM_TEST_DB_URL not set — skipping DB test' followed by a bare 'failed command: ./.zig-cache/o/.../test --cache-dir=./.zig-cache --seed=0xad9f7012 --listen=-' line with no summary/pass-count line, then after a ~5 minute gap the loop logged 'zig build test attempt 1 failed or timed out (exit 124)' (the timeout(1) wrapper firing, matching ISS-0136's documented hang). Attempt 2 (immediately after) printed the EXACT SAME shape of output -- 16x skip lines, then 'failed command: .../test --cache-dir=... --seed=0x58abf9f1 --listen=-' -- but this time the loop's 'if [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; then exit 0; fi' branch fired: no 'attempt 2 failed' message was ever printed, and the workflow proceeded straight to the next step ('transition.zig in-file tests'). The job's overall conclusion was 'success'. A human reviewing the raw log (not just the green checkmark) flagged this: attempt 2's own output shows what looks like a Zig build-graph failure line, which is not what a clean pass looks like.
reproduction: Consistently reproducible on GitHub Actions' Ubuntu runner (not on local Windows dev machines) -- observed on 3 independent CI runs during this issue's own investigation. To inspect: `gh run view <run-id> --job <job-id> --log` for any recent 'Build and unit tests' job and search for 'failed command:'.
root_cause_analysis: TWO ROUND OF INVESTIGATION, second round corrects the first: ROUND 1 (initial, INCORRECT hypothesis): assumed `zig build`'s top-level exit code could come back 0 even though a child Run step (an individual test binary) genuinely failed -- i.e. that error propagation to the top-level exit code was unreliable under -j2 contention. This led to a first fix that treated any 'failed command:' line as a hard failure regardless of exit code. ROUND 2 (correct root cause, found by re-running the ROUND-1 fix for real on CI with `--summary all` added for diagnostics): the 'failed command:' line is NOT evidence of a real failure. Every CI run exhibiting it also printed 'Build Summary: 38/38 steps succeeded; NNN/701 tests passed' moments later, with every leaf in the full --summary-all tree showing a genuine `success` (fresh compile+run with real timing/MaxRSS data) or `cached` status -- i.e. the run demonstrably passed in full, 3 times in a row across 3 attempts within the same CI run, each with a different --seed. The 'failed command:' line consistently appears immediately after a '+- run test w' (w = waiting) live-progress-bar line and never after a real result line, and never appears at all on a local run in a real TTY. This is strong evidence that 'failed command:' is a stale/speculative frame from Zig 0.16's live progress-bar renderer -- a frame a real terminal overwrites in place via ANSI cursor movement, but which a non-TTY CI log (GitHub Actions captures raw stdout, no terminal emulation) preserves as permanent, misleading text. This is a Zig 0.16 build-runner COSMETIC / non-TTY-output bug, not a genuine build or test failure, and is unrelated to ISS-0136/GH #436's actual -j2 concurrency deadlock (which manifests as a true hang -> timeout(1) killing the process at exit 124, with NO 'Build Summary' line ever printed -- that failure mode is real and remains correctly handled by this loop).
impact: The CI 'Build and unit tests' job's green checkmark cannot currently be trusted as proof that `zig build test` actually passed under the OLD (pre-fix) loop logic -- it may only prove that the LAST of up to 3 attempts didn't get killed by `timeout(1)`, even if that attempt's own output contained a misleading 'failed command:' artifact line. This was observed directly on PR #447 (merged with this CI job green) for the ISS-0139/ISS-0140 fix -- separately, `zig build test` was independently re-run and verified locally (twice) during that PR's development with real, visible pass/fail counts (616/701 and 617/701, 1 unrelated pre-existing flaky failure each time, see ISS-0141/GH #445), so PR #447's actual code change is NOT believed to be broken. IMPORTANT CORRECTION: the FIRST fix attempted for this issue (treating any 'failed command:' line as a hard failure) was ITSELF WRONG and would have made CI permanently red on every genuinely passing run going forward -- caught only because the fix's own PR (#449) was watched through a REAL CI run and its log read in full rather than trusting the checkmark, per direct user feedback during this investigation ('Isn't it crazy to wait... Isn't the second attempt marked OK when it's not?' followed by catching the corrected fix's own new false-negative). See resolution for the corrected, verified approach.
acceptance_criteria: Determine definitively why 'failed command:' appears despite a genuine pass -- DONE: root-caused to Zig 0.16's live progress-bar renderer leaving a stale 'w' (waiting)-state frame in non-TTY output; NOT a build-graph failure

Harden the retry loop in .github/workflows/ci.yml so a cosmetic 'failed command:' artifact cannot cause a false failure, while still catching genuine partial failures and genuine hangs -- DONE: parse the 'Build Summary: N/N steps succeeded' line and require N == N for PASS; a hang (no Build Summary line ever printed) or a genuine partial failure (N < N) is still correctly caught

Add a regression test/dry-run that deliberately induces the cosmetic-artifact-with-genuine-pass condition, a genuine-failure condition, and a genuine-hang condition, and confirms the corrected loop distinguishes all three -- DONE via local bash simulation (not committed as a repo test file; exercises shell control flow, not Zig/Python source)

Once fixed, re-run CI on a currently-open or new PR and confirm the retry loop's log output includes a real pass/fail summary line on every attempt -- DONE: verified on 3 separate real CI runs during this investigation (PR #447's original run understood retroactively; PR #449's two re-runs directly observed)
resolution: Final, verified fix in .github/workflows/ci.yml's 'zig build test' retry loop: `--summary all` is now passed to `zig build test` so a structured 'Build Summary: N/N steps succeeded' line is always printed on completion (not just on failure, which is the default 'failures' summary mode). Each attempt's output is captured via `tee` + `${PIPESTATUS[0]}`, and the loop parses that Build Summary line's N/N -- PASS requires the line to exist AND its two numbers to be equal. This correctly ignores the cosmetic 'failed command:' progress-bar artifact (which appears on every attempt regardless of outcome) while still catching genuine partial failures (N < N) and genuine hangs (timeout(1) kills the process before any Build Summary line is ever printed, exit 124, matching ISS-0136/GH #436's real concurrency issue). NOTE: an intermediate, INCORRECT fix (matching on the mere presence of a 'failed command:' line) was committed, pushed, and observed to fail CI in real time before this corrected version replaced it -- see root_cause_analysis for why that intermediate approach was wrong. The corrected fix was itself verified against a real, passing CI run before merge.
evidence_file: N/A -- see symptom/root_cause_analysis fields; full raw logs available via gh run view for runs 31033090698 (PR #447, original discovery), 31034287986 and 31035290642 (PR #449, root-cause correction)
